title: ReactorBuilder uses a fluent API to wire storage, executors, read models, sync, and document models into a reactor instance
content:
The `ReactorBuilder` from `@powerhousedao/reactor` provides a fluent API for constructing reactors: `withDocumentModelSources(sources)` (which accepts live document-model modules, importable `{ filePath }` files, and importable `{ packageName }` packages), `withExecutorConfig({ maxConcurrency, jobTimeoutMs })`, `withWriteCacheConfig({ maxDocuments, ringBufferSize })`, `withMigrationStrategy('auto')`, `withKysely()` (defaults to in-memory PGlite), `withQueue()` (defaults to InMemoryQueue), `withEventBus()`, `withReadModel()`, `withSync()`, and more. Calling `build()` returns `IReactor`; calling `buildModule()` returns an `InProcessReactorModule` exposing all internal components including operationStore, keyframeStore, writeCache, documentView, documentIndexer, readModelCoordinator, processorManager, and the underlying Kysely database. The base `ReactorModule` interface it extends carries only three fields (`documentModelRegistry`, `syncModule`, `eventBus`) — the subset a client can resolve regardless of where the reactor graph lives.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: The builder pattern configures maxConcurrency, write cache, migration strategy, Kysely DB, queues, event bus, and sync for reactor construction.
